scope: Numerical and cross-code checks of the radiation calculation. They establish implementation correctness and discretisation accuracy for the stated configurations; they do not validate the prescribed column structure, the absence of clouds or any lunar climate outcome.
unit_tests: atmosphere/tests/test_radiative_convective.py (21 tests: thermodynamic limits, analytic radiative transfer, two-stream conservation and doubling, MT_CKD port against AER example output, multi-mesh line kernel against direct Voigt sums, CIA precedence, Rayleigh optical depth, solar spectrum total, CO2 node table against direct calculation)

monte_carlo_rayleigh.description: Two-stream (PIFM) direct-beam reflectance of a conservative Rayleigh slab over a black surface against a 400,000-photon Monte Carlo with the Rayleigh phase function (scratch reference, statistical 1-sigma about 0.001).
monte_carlo_rayleigh.conclusion: Two-stream reflectance is low by 0.1-3%; for the lunar Rayleigh optical depths this is about 0.003 in planetary albedo (about 1 W/m2).

pyrads.description: PyRADS (Koll & Cronin 2018; MIT licence; commit of 2024-01-17) run with its own saturated H2O-N2 profiles (60 levels, 0.01 cm-1, T_strat 200 K, dry surface pressure 1e5 Pa, Voigt lines, MT_CKD 3.2, main H2O isotopologue, diffusivity 5/3). This model was run on the same profiles with constant gravity, water lines and continuum only, and the same diffusivity.
pyrads.conclusion: With PyRADS data choices (MT_CKD 3.2, main isotopologue) this code reproduces PyRADS OLR within 0.4% at Earth and lunar gravity from 250 to 360 K. The default configuration (MT_CKD 4.3, all isotopologues) differs from PyRADS by up to +2.2% in hot saturated columns, almost entirely from the continuum version (+7 W/m2 at 340 K, Earth gravity); isotopologues contribute -2 W/m2. That spread is a data uncertainty of the runaway limit.

convergence.case: Moon, 1.2 atm dry, 400 ppm CO2, Manabe-Wetherald humidity, Ts 288 K, T_strat 200 K (and a saturated 340 K column for the line floor)
convergence.conclusion: Spectral step, angles, line-intensity floor, solar zenith nodes and solar levels change the budget by less than 0.03 W/m2. Vertical discretisation of the thermal calculation converges at first order: the standard 70+20 levels read OLR about 0.6 W/m2 low (Richardson estimate from 45+12, 70+20 and 140+40 levels). The pseudo-spherical beam raises ASR by 1.8 W/m2 over plane-parallel.

table_interpolation: CO2 node table against direct calculation: under 1% at any wavenumber, 0.3% in band integrals; OLR of an Earth column changes by 0.01 W/m2.
